message.content:
You are applying a page-entry animation cascade to the PROPERTY desktop pages of the TaptPay app at /home/runner/workspace.

## Files you own (edit ONLY these four)
- client/src/desktop/pages/property-home.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/property-clients.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/property-terminal.tsx
- client/src/desktop/pages/property-analytics.tsx

Do NOT edit any other file. In particular do NOT edit client/src/desktop/desktop.css, client/src/App.tsx, or any shared component — other agents own those and I own the shared CSS.

## Context
The tablet/desktop app frame + header + nav are now mounted persistently ABOVE the router, so navigating between screens no longer remounts the chrome. Only the page slot swaps. That means the incoming page's own entry animation IS the page transition. The user's requirement, verbatim: "all componants on every page needs to have a smooth bounce pop in transition with a cascading effect".

## The primitives (already exist in client/src/desktop/desktop.css — read it first, do not modify it)
- `@keyframes desktopBounceIn` — a bounce settle with three decaying overshoots.
- `.dt-rise` — applies desktopBounceIn. Delay = `var(--dt-i, 0) * 52ms + var(--dt-d, 0ms)`.
- `.dt-cascade` — put on a container; auto-assigns `--dt-i` 0..9 to its DIRECT children via nth-child.

Use `.dt-cascade` on a layout container when its direct children are the blocks you want to sequence. Use `.dt-rise` with an explicit `style={{ "--dt-i": 3 } as CSSProperties}` when you need control over ordering across separate containers (e.g. a two-column layout where you want left column then right column).

## What to change
Each of these pages currently animates its top-level layout blocks with `popIn` or `tileIn` at hand-written delays (search for `animation:popIn` and `animation:tileIn` in the styled-template strings). Convert the TOP-LEVEL SCREEN COMPOSITION blocks to the new cascade so the whole screen reads as one sequence, in natural reading order (hero/headline first, then chart, then supporting strips, then lists, then side panels).

Rules:
1. ONLY convert animations that play when the SCREEN FIRST APPEARS. Leave alone any `tileIn`/`reportIn`/`popIn` that fires on an in-page state change — modals, scrims, sheets, report renders, expanded detail panels, bars growing when a filter changes. Those are interactions, not page entry. If you are unsure whether something is entry or interaction, leave it as it is and say so in your report.
2. Do not change layout, geometry, spacing, colors, copy, or behaviour. Animation only.
3. Do not add any animation library. No framer-motion. CSS only — this is an explicit project rule.
4. Do not add a `prefers-reduced-motion` block; desktop.css already neutralises all animation inside `.tapt-desktop-viewport` globally.
5. Keep the cascade short enough to feel snappy: the last element should start no later than ~450ms. If a screen has more than ~9 entry blocks, group them so the tail does not drag.
6. These are real trading screens (property-terminal sends rent requests). Do not touch any query, mutation, handler, or state logic.

## Verify before reporting
For each file you changed, run a syntax check:
  cd /home/runner/workspace && npx esbuild <file> --loader=tsx --outfile=/dev/null
All four must pass. Do NOT run `npx tsc` (project-wide, slow, and I run it centrally).

## Report back
A concise list: per file, which blocks you sequenced and in what order, and anything you deliberately left alone (with the reason). Flag anything that looked like a pre-existing bug — do not fix it.

content.text:
All four files pass `esbuild`. Summary:

## client/src/desktop/pages/property-home.tsx
`.ph-left` and `.ph-right` became `dt-cascade` containers; the eight hand-written `popIn` delays were removed. `.ph-right` carries `--dt-d:208ms` so the right column continues the left column's count instead of restarting.

Order (0→8, last at 416ms): scope pill → hero amount → bar chart + range chips → breakdown card → portfolio health → notifications → search row → tenants list → quick actions.

Left alone: `.ph-hdet` (`tileIn`) — plays when you tap a health number to open the detail panel; interaction, not entry. Note the scope pill now animates where it previously didn't — it is the first block in reading order and looked wrong sitting still while everything under it rose.

## client/src/desktop/pages/property-clients.tsx
Four explicit `dt-rise` blocks with `--dt-i` set in the page CSS (0→3, last at 156ms): scope pill → active-tenant count hero → search + add row → tenant list.

Left alone: `.pc-modal` (`tileIn`) — the add-tenant modal, an interaction. `DesktopDirectoryProfile` was left untouched deliberately: it mounts on tenant selection (interaction), and it is a shared component owned by another agent — so I did **not** put `dt-cascade` on `.pc-body`, which would have swept it in.

## client/src/desktop/pages/property-terminal.tsx
`.pt-left` became a `dt-cascade` (its `popIn` removed), so its six blocks run steps 0–5 individually rather than the whole column arriving as one slab; then `.pt-rail` (`--dt-i:6`) and `.pt-panel` (`--dt-i:7`) complete a left-to-right sweep. Last starts at 364ms.

Order: scope pill → outstanding-rent figure → its label → outstanding-expenses figure → its label → request stack (search/chips/rows) → tool rail → right panel.

Notes: I animated `.pt-rail` itself, **not** `.pt-rail-slot` — the rail is `position:absolute` against `.pt-body`, and a transform on the slot would have made the slot its containing block and moved it. The hero figures are bare sibling spans in a flex column with no wrapper; I animated them individually rather than adding a wrapper div, which would have reintroduced margin collapsing. No query/mutation/handler was touched.

Left alone: `.pt-mode` (`tileIn`) — replays on every rail mode switch (tenant/request/keypad/bill/paid), so it is an interaction. It now plays underneath `.pt-panel`'s rise on first paint, which reads fine (content is settled by the time the panel arrives).

## client/src/desktop/pages/property-analytics.tsx
This page had **no** entry animation at all — every existing animation here is interaction-driven. I added one: `.pa-overview-head` and `.pa-hero-col` as `dt-cascade` containers (the latter with `--dt-d:104ms` to continue the count), and `.pa-chart` as `dt-rise --dt-i:6`.

Order (0→6, last at 312ms): scope pill → range tabs → total-revenue figure + growth pill → "total revenue" label → outstanding figure → its label → revenue chart.

**Deliberately left alone, two of them for correctness rather than taste:**
- `.pa-sheet` (payment-history bottom sheet) — it is driven by an inline `transform: translateY(${sheetY}px)` for the drag. `desktopBounceIn` animates `transform` with `both`, so the forwards fill would pin it at `translateY(0)` permanently and **break the drag/expand**. It cannot join the cascade without a fade-only keyframe, which would mean touching shared CSS. Flagging for you.
- `.pa-dot` (the white peak marker) — centred by `transform: translate(-50%,-50%)`. The same forwards fill would clobber that and leave the dot permanently offset by half its size. Left static.
- `.pa-report` (`reportIn`), `.pa-bar` (`tileIn`), `.pa-tiles-wrap`, `.pa-filters` — all fire on report generation or sheet mode changes; interactions.

One accepted side-effect worth knowing: the overview is inside `{!report && …}`, so pressing "back" from a generated report now remounts it and replays the 312ms cascade. Previously that was instant. It reads as a re-entry and matches `reportIn` in the other direction, but say the word and I'll gate it.

No pre-existing bugs spotted in these four files beyond the two transform conflicts above, which are latent traps rather than live bugs. No layout, geometry, copy, or logic changed anywhere.
